questions.stem: Commerce is defined as the study of how
options: man utilizes the resources in his physical environment
man produces, distributes and consumes his goods and services
man buys, sells and distributes goods and services
raw materials are changed into finished goods
questions.explanation: Commerce covers the buying, selling and distribution of goods and services (trade and aids to trade).

questions.stem: The type of activity which turns processed raw materials into consumer and industrial goods is described as
questions.explanation: Manufacturing (secondary production) converts processed raw materials into consumer and producer goods.

questions.stem: The production process that combines two or more raw materials into one end product is
questions.explanation: Synthetic manufacturing combines several raw materials into a single finished product.

questions.stem: A demonstration of social responsibility by a business is the payment of
questions.explanation: Paying taxes contributes to public services for society; dividends, interest and premiums are contractual obligations to specific parties.

questions.stem: A distinguishing characteristic of a limited liability company is that it
options: is a collection of many sole proprietors
questions.explanation: A company is a separate legal entity, so it can sue and be sued in its own name.

questions.stem: Which of the following takes place when firms producing at different stages in the same industry combine?
questions.explanation: Combining firms at different stages of the same production chain is vertical integration.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups is paid first when a firm liquidates?
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are creditors of the company and are paid before any class of shareholders.

questions.stem: Compulsory dissolution of a business can arise from
options: a declaration by a court of law
questions.explanation: Compulsory dissolution (winding up) is ordered by a court; dissolution by agreement is voluntary.

questions.stem: Use the data below to answer the question. MBV Enterprises, Balance Sheet as at 31st December, 1992. Liabilities: Capital - balance as at Jan. 1, 1992 N60,000; add net profit N5,250 = N65,250; less drawings N6,600 = N58,650. Current liabilities: Creditors N9,730. Total N68,380. Assets: Fixed assets - Fittings N9,200, Vehicles N7,500 = N16,700. Current assets - Stock in hand N8,800, Debtors N15,500, Cash at bank N21,000, Cash in hand N6,380 = N51,680. Total N68,380. What is the circulating capital of the sole proprietor?
questions.explanation: Circulating capital = current assets = 8,800 + 15,500 + 21,000 + 6,380 = N51,680.

questions.stem: Use the data below to answer the question. MBV Enterprises, Balance Sheet as at 31st December, 1992. What is the working capital as at December 31, 1992?
questions.explanation: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities = 51,680 - 9,730 = N41,950.

questions.stem: A company earned a total revenue of N108 million with a total cost of N91 million in 1991. If it paid 45% tax on its gross profit for that year, determine its net profit.
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 108 - 91 = N17m; tax = 45% of 17 = N7.65m; net profit = 17 - 7.65 = N9.35m.

questions.stem: What are fixtures and fittings in a balance sheet?
questions.explanation: Fixtures and fittings are held for long-term use in the business, so they are fixed assets.

questions.stem: Government impose import duties for the following reasons EXCEPT
options: to raise revenue for other services
to act as a retaliatory measure against other governments
to discourage the redistribution of income at home
to protect home industries from external competition
questions.explanation: Import duties raise revenue, retaliate and protect home industries; discouraging income redistribution is not a reason for them.

questions.stem: Sole enterprise may flourish best in
questions.explanation: Retailing needs little capital and personal attention, which suits a sole trader; the others need huge capital.

questions.stem: The use of coin-operated machines to sell goods is a form of
questions.explanation: Vending (coin-operated) machines sell in small quantities to final consumers - a form of retailing.

questions.stem: What is the major function of the wholesaler?
options: Buying from small-scale producers and selling to exporters
Buying in bulk and selling in small quantities
Granting of credit facilities to retailers
Providing information to manufacturers on market situation
questions.explanation: The wholesaler's main function is breaking bulk: buying in large quantities from producers and selling in smaller lots to retailers.

questions.stem: The rate at which a country's exports exchange for its imports is called
questions.explanation: Terms of trade measure the rate at which a country's exports exchange for its imports (index of export prices over import prices).

questions.stem: The difference between the total payments for imports and the receipts from exports within a given period is referred to as
questions.explanation: The balance of trade is the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of goods over a period.

questions.stem: A pro forma invoice is NOT required when
options: quoting for the supply of goods
questions.explanation: A pro forma invoice is used for quotations, goods on approval or uncertain prices; it is unnecessary for a regular customer on normal credit terms.

questions.stem: The postal organization which preceded the Nigerian Postal Service is
questions.explanation: NIPOST was created in 1985 when the old Post and Telecommunications (P&T) department was split into NIPOST and NITEL.

questions.stem: Goods discharged from ships on which import duties have not been paid are kept in the
questions.explanation: Bonded warehouses hold imported goods until customs duties are paid.

questions.stem: A sole proprietor insured his goods worth N200,000 for half the value. There was a fire incident in which goods valued at N80,000 were destroyed. The value of compensation expected from the insurer is
questions.explanation: Under the average clause for under-insurance: 100,000/200,000 x 80,000 = N40,000.

questions.stem: One of the effects of the devaluation of the Naira is that the
options: goods that can be imported with the Naira have become cheaper
value of other currencies relative to the Naira have become cheaper
goods that can be exported from Nigeria have become costlier
imports that can be bought with the Naira have become costlier
questions.explanation: Devaluation lowers the external value of the Naira, so more Naira is needed to buy imports - imports become costlier.

questions.stem: Drawing two parallel lines across a cheque means that it has to be paid into the account of the
questions.explanation: A crossed cheque cannot be cashed over the counter; it must be paid into the payee's bank account.

questions.stem: The financial institution established to boost Nigeria's trade with the rest of the world is called
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM) was set up to finance and promote Nigeria's foreign trade.

questions.stem: Which of the following is both direct and indirect credit enterprises?
questions.explanation: Co-operative thrift and credit societies both collect savings and give credit to members directly and indirectly.

questions.stem: The Second-Tier Securities Market is
options: an appendage to the Nigerian Stock Exchange
a member of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
meant for the shares of the quoted private companies
a regulating arm of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
questions.explanation: The Second-Tier Securities Market (1985) is a section attached to the Nigerian Stock Exchange for small and medium-sized companies.

questions.stem: The elements of the marketing mix are
questions.explanation: The marketing mix is the 4Ps: product, price, place and promotion.

questions.stem: Which of the following items has the shortest effect on the consumer?
questions.explanation: A fad is a short-lived craze, shorter than a fashion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of sales promotion?
questions.explanation: Free samples are a sales promotion technique; radio and TV are advertising media.

questions.stem: One advantage of personal selling over all other elements of promotion is that
options: it is very cheap in terms of cost per contact
it does not need to use mass media
questions.explanation: Face-to-face selling gets immediate feedback from the buyer; it is actually the most expensive per contact.

questions.stem: Which of the following must be present in an agency by agreement?
questions.explanation: Agency by agreement arises from the mutual consent of principal and agent.

questions.stem: An agreement to sell is distinguishable from a sale because in the former, the transfer of goods is
questions.explanation: In an agreement to sell, transfer of ownership is to take place at a future time; in a sale it passes immediately.

questions.stem: Mr. Amusa says to Mr Bello 'I will sell you this hat for N30'. And Mr Bello replied 'I will pay N29'. The contract is
questions.explanation: Bello's reply is a counter-offer, which rejects the original offer, so there is no acceptance.

questions.stem: Nationalization of an industry means that its ownership becomes that of
questions.explanation: Nationalization transfers ownership of an enterprise to the government (state).

questions.stem: The Comprehensive Import Supervision Scheme was set up by the federal government in order to
options: promote fair trade between Nigeria and other countries
counteract all fraudulent business deals of Nigerians with other nationals
ensure that imports into Nigeria are of the correct quality, value and quantity
questions.explanation: CISS involved pre-shipment inspection to verify the quality, quantity and price of imports.

questions.stem: Which of the following has powers to order withdrawal of a particular food item from circulation?
options: Food and Drugs Department of the Federal Ministry of Health
questions.explanation: Under the Food and Drugs Act, the Food and Drugs Department of the Federal Ministry of Health could order unsafe food withdrawn (as at 1994).

questions.stem: NACCIMA stands for
options: Nigerian-American Centre for Culture, Industries, Mines and Arts
Nigerian Association for Culture, Civics, Industries, Minerals and Arts
National Agency for Culture, Civilization, Investments, Manufacturing and Agriculture
Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture
questions.explanation: NACCIMA is the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture.

questions.stem: The harmonious relationship among the various units in an organization is ensured through
questions.explanation: Co-ordination harmonises the activities of the various units towards common goals.

questions.stem: The principle of span of control stipulates that
options: an employee should report to only one superior
managers must demand accountability from their subordinates
resources have to be economized within the various divisions
the number of employees reporting to one superior should be kept to a workable maximum
questions.explanation: Span of control limits the number of subordinates a superior can effectively supervise; option A is unity of command.

questions.stem: The use of computers in modern banking industry is a reflection of
questions.explanation: Computerisation of banking reflects technological development.

questions.stem: When an oil exploring and mining company builds a health centre in one of the communities where it operates, such a company is
options: finding a way to spend excess profits
fulfilling part of its social responsibility
questions.explanation: Providing amenities for host communities is part of a firm's social responsibility.

questions.stem: The West African Clearing House became legally operational on
questions.explanation: The West African Clearing House agreement was signed in March 1975 and the House began operations on 1st July 1976.

questions.stem: The Lake Chad Basin Commission was founded to enable member states
options: expand the volume of water in the Lake for fishing activity
increase navigational activities on the lake
dam the lake for electricity and agricultural purposes
co-ordinate their efforts in managing the use of the lake's resources
questions.explanation: The Lake Chad Basin Commission (1964) co-ordinates member states' use and management of the lake basin's resources.

questions.stem: What are the factors with which commercial undertakings can be distinguished? I. Size of the undertakings. II. Profits generated. III. Forms of ownership. IV. Location of the undertakings.
questions.explanation: Business undertakings are classified by size and by form of ownership (sole, partnership, company, public).

questions.stem: In which of the following sets of occupations can an industrial worker be found?
questions.explanation: Industrial occupations are extraction, manufacturing and construction; commerce, banking and insurance are not industrial.

questions.stem: Construction activities include the building of houses and roads as well as
questions.explanation: Bricklaying is a construction activity; the others are manufacturing activities.

questions.stem: If a partnership deed is silent on how profits are to be shared, partners share profits
options: in the ratio of the value of business secured by each partner for the partnership
in the ratio of partners' capital contributions
in an equal proportion, irrespective of partners' capital contributions
according to duties performed by each partner
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership Act, in the absence of agreement profits and losses are shared equally.

questions.stem: Which of the following information is contained in the Articles of Association of a limited liability company?
questions.explanation: The Articles govern internal management, including directors' powers and duties; the others are in the Memorandum.

questions.stem: The merger of two companies producing the same type of products is an example of
questions.explanation: Combining firms at the same stage producing similar products is horizontal integration.

questions.stem: One of the implications of the incorporation of a company is that
options: it is more difficult for the company to raise loans
the company can sue but cannot be sued
the company's property becomes distinguished from that of its members
its members become liable for all the debts of the company
questions.explanation: Incorporation makes the company a separate legal person whose property is distinct from its members'.

questions.stem: The main advantage of a sole trader is the freedom to
options: plough all the profits back into the business
questions.explanation: Being sole owner and manager, the sole trader can take decisions promptly without consulting anyone.

questions.stem: In the case of voluntary liquidation of a business, the receiver is appointed by the
questions.explanation: In a members' voluntary winding up, the shareholders in general meeting appoint the liquidator (receiver).

questions.stem: When a company uses more of loans than equity to finance its business, the company is said to be
questions.explanation: A high proportion of debt to equity capital means high gearing.

questions.stem: A public limited company can raise long-term loans through
questions.explanation: Long-term funds are raised on the capital market; the money market, overdrafts and discount houses supply short-term funds.

questions.stem: The financial index which compares current assets directly with current liabilities is known as current
questions.explanation: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities.

questions.stem: Rights issue means the
options: issue of shares to the directors of a company on favourable terms
issue of shares by a company only to the founders of the company
right of shareholders to vote on any issue
issue of shares to shareholders on favourable terms
questions.explanation: A rights issue offers new shares to existing shareholders, usually at a price below market, in proportion to their holdings.

questions.stem: Profit that is expressed as a percentage of the cost of goods sold is referred to as
questions.explanation: Mark-up is profit as a percentage of cost; margin is profit as a percentage of selling price.

questions.stem: Given: Opening stock N40,000; Purchases N115,000; Closing stock N60,000; Sales N250,000. What is the cost of goods sold?
In the channel of distribution, which of the following sets is entirely made up of middlemen?
questions.explanation: Middlemen stand between producer and consumer: wholesalers, retailers and agents.

questions.stem: Goods imported into a country for the purpose of re-exporting attracts a rebate known as
questions.explanation: A customs drawback is the refund of import duty on goods that are re-exported.

questions.stem: Most foreign trade transactions are paid for through the use of
options: bank drafts drawn by commercial banks on their foreign branches
irrevocable and confirmed letters of credit
letters of credit authenticated by the embassies of the respective countries
questions.explanation: Irrevocable confirmed letters of credit guarantee payment to the exporter and are the usual means of settling foreign trade.

questions.stem: RRF as a scheme introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria means
questions.explanation: The CBN's RRF is the Refinancing and Rediscounting Facility for banks' loans to priority sectors.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives the correct order in which the listed documents are used?
options: Debit note, order, delivery note, invoice and statement
Order, delivery note, invoice, debit note and statement
Statement, order, invoice, delivery note and statement
Invoice, order, statement, debit note and delivery note
questions.explanation: The buyer orders first; goods come with a delivery note, then the invoice, any debit note for undercharges, and finally the statement of account.

questions.stem: Freight note is a document
options: used by government to transport goods from one country to another
issued by a shipping company giving details of charges
used for payment for imported goods
given by an importer to pay for goods at a future period
questions.explanation: A freight note is the shipping company's bill showing the freight charges payable.

questions.stem: An invoice of N600 is marked '5% 1 month', '2½% 3 months' and '1% 5 months'. If a customer pays in the second month of purchase, how much will he remit to the seller?
questions.explanation: Payment in the second month earns the 2½% cash discount: 600 - 15 = N585.

questions.stem: Spot market goods are those which are available for
questions.explanation: Spot goods are sold for immediate delivery and payment, unlike futures.

questions.stem: The main advantage of road transport is that it is
questions.explanation: Road transport offers door-to-door service and flexible routes and timing.

questions.stem: The practice by which an insurance company accepts a very large risk and later shares it with other insurance companies is called
questions.explanation: Re-insurance is when an insurer passes part of a large risk to other insurers.

questions.stem: The insurance policy which provides full cover against all risks at sea is known as
questions.explanation: A With Particular Average policy covers both total and partial losses, giving the widest cover of those listed; FPA excludes partial losses.

questions.stem: Berne Union is also known as
options: International Union of Credit and Investment Insurers
questions.explanation: The Berne Union is the International Union of Credit and Investment Insurers.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of items was used for exchange in Nigeria before money was introduced?
options: Cowries, iron rods, brass rods and copper wires
Iron rods, copper rods, manilla and cowries
Cowries, manilla, brass rods and copper wires
Copper wires, brass wires, cowries, and iron rods
questions.explanation: Traditional currencies in Nigeria included cowries, manillas, brass rods and copper wires.

questions.stem: A major liability of a commercial bank arises from
questions.explanation: Deposits are owed to customers, so they are the bank's main liability; loans and overdrafts are assets.

questions.stem: A bank statement is a document
options: ordering a bank to pay on demand a stated sum of money
containing records of receipts, payments and balance on an account
used for paying money into a bank account
used for regular withdrawal of money from a savings account
questions.explanation: A bank statement records deposits, withdrawals and the balance of a customer's account.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the stock exchange market?
options: Providing long-term loans to large scale enterprises
Encouraging people to buy shares and thereby providing capital for investment
Providing means of assessing the value of a firm's assets
Enabling firms to wind-up quickly in times of difficulties
questions.explanation: The stock exchange mobilises long-term capital and values securities; helping firms wind up is not one of its functions.

questions.stem: The breaking down of a market into separate and identifiable elements each with its own special product requirements is known as market
questions.explanation: Market segmentation divides a market into distinct groups of buyers with different needs.

questions.stem: Taking a new product to a particular part of a country to test the reaction of consumers to the product is referred to as
questions.explanation: Sampling tests consumers' reaction to a new product in a selected area before full launch.

questions.stem: A manufacturer can make his product distinguishable from those of other competitors by
options: selling the product at a much lower price
questions.explanation: Branding and packaging give a product a distinct identity from competitors'.

questions.stem: Which of the following are forms of sales promotion?
questions.explanation: Advertising, personal selling and publicity are elements of promotion; skimming is a pricing policy and packaging is part of the product.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of personal selling is that it
options: increases a company's number of customers
reduces a company's area of patronage
questions.explanation: Personal selling is costly because of salesmen's salaries, commissions and travel.

questions.stem: Consumer sovereignty means that the consumer is
questions.explanation: Consumer sovereignty holds that the consumer is 'king' - his choices direct what is produced - expressed as 'the customer is always right'.

questions.stem: When an industry or company is nationalized, the state becomes
options: an equal shareholder with other individuals
questions.explanation: Nationalization transfers full ownership to the state.

questions.stem: The Federal Government made efforts at rendering public enterprises more efficient and profit-oriented through the process of
questions.explanation: Commercialization keeps public enterprises in government hands but requires them to run on profit-oriented lines.

questions.stem: Which of the following organizations represents those who engage labour in Nigeria?
options: Nigerian Union of Local Government Employees
questions.explanation: NECA is the umbrella body of employers of labour in Nigeria; the NLC represents workers.

questions.stem: The practice of assessing employees for payment or advancement according to their observed achievement is called
questions.explanation: Merit rating appraises employees' performance as a basis for pay and promotion.

questions.stem: Motivation is an essential element in management because it
options: leads to the improvement of staff welfare
encourages individuals to work towards achieving the organisation's objectives
reduces friction among employees in the process of achieving the organization's objectives
questions.explanation: Motivation induces workers to put in effort towards the organisation's goals.

questions.stem: The direct authority of a superior over his subordinate is known as
questions.explanation: Line authority is the direct chain of command from superior to subordinate.

questions.stem: A firm's organisational structure would change if
options: one of the major partners dies
there is seasonal variation in demand
the scope of business operation changes
questions.explanation: Structure follows the scope of operations; expanding or contracting activities requires reorganisation.

questions.stem: The secretariat of the Niger Basin Commission is located at
questions.explanation: The Niger Basin Commission (now Authority) has its headquarters in Niamey, Niger.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the components of commerce? I. Trading and advertising II. Warehousing and transportation III. Packaging and branding IV. Insurance and banking.
questions.explanation: Commerce consists of trade and aids to trade (advertising, warehousing, transport, insurance, banking); packaging and branding belong to production/marketing.

questions.stem: A royal charter was granted to the Royal Niger Company to do business in Nigeria in
questions.explanation: The National African Company received its royal charter as the Royal Niger Company in July 1886.

questions.stem: An example of indirect service is rendered by
questions.explanation: Indirect services are rendered to the public through an employer such as government (civil servants); doctors, servants and entertainers serve people directly.

questions.stem: The objectives of a business are determined by the
questions.explanation: The promoters (founders/owners) set the objectives when forming the business.

questions.stem: Partnerships are most suitable where
options: members can easily raise enough capital
questions.explanation: Professional firms (lawyers, accountants, doctors) are typically organised as partnerships.

questions.stem: The business organization in which shareholders have equal votes is
questions.explanation: Co-operatives operate on 'one member, one vote' regardless of shares held.

questions.stem: The major objective of corporate mergers is to
questions.explanation: Firms merge mainly to enjoy economies of large-scale operation.

questions.stem: When it becomes necessary to liquidate a company, the first step to be taken is the appointment of
questions.explanation: Winding up begins with the appointment of a liquidator to realise assets and pay creditors.

questions.stem: In which of the following circumstances is a court order NOT necessary for the winding up of a company?
options: Suspension of business for one year
Reduction in the number of members below the legal minimum
questions.explanation: A special resolution of members leads to voluntary winding up without a court order; the others are grounds for compulsory winding up by the court.

questions.stem: One type of investment that has a variable income is
questions.explanation: Ordinary share dividends vary with profits; debentures, bonds and preference shares carry fixed returns.

questions.stem: Leasing is the right to use assets for an agreed period in return for
questions.explanation: The lessee pays rentals to the lessor for the use of the asset.

questions.stem: The form of business financing which involves pledging of a specific asset is
questions.explanation: A mortgage is a loan secured on a specific property pledged as collateral.

questions.stem: The total amount that a company is allowed to raise according to its memorandum of association is known as
questions.explanation: Authorized (nominal) capital is the maximum share capital stated in the memorandum.

questions.stem: A public limited liability company having a nominal capital made up of 200 000 ordinary shares of 50k each decided to issue 50% of it to the public. What is the authorized capital?
questions.explanation: Authorized capital = 200,000 x N0.50 = N100,000; the amount issued does not change it.

questions.stem: The turnover of a firm may be affected by
options: the cost of its goods sold
questions.explanation: Turnover is the value of sales, which depends on the demand for the product.

questions.stem: The cost of transporting goods to customers is called
questions.explanation: Carriage outwards is the cost of delivering goods sold to customers.

questions.stem: In foreign trade, document of title is known as
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is the document of title to goods shipped by sea.

questions.stem: Excise duties are paid on goods that are
questions.explanation: Excise duties are taxes on locally manufactured goods.

questions.stem: Stevedores as a term in foreign trade means men who
questions.explanation: Stevedores are dock workers who load and unload ships.

questions.stem: A close indent is an instruction to an agent to
options: order goods from a particular manufacturer
sell goods to a certain firm
questions.explanation: A closed (specific) indent names the particular manufacturer to buy from; an open indent leaves the choice to the agent.

questions.stem: The basic distinction between cash discount and trade discount is that while trade discount is
options: for a period of 30 days, cash discount is for a period of 3 months
given by a wholesaler, cash discount is given by a bank
a reduction in the catalogue price of an article, cash discount is a reduction in the invoice value
a reduction in value of sales, cash discount is a reduction in price of goods
questions.explanation: Trade discount is deducted from the list (catalogue) price; cash discount reduces the invoice amount for prompt payment.

questions.stem: The cost that arises from failure to load or unload a ship at the port within a stipulated period is known as
questions.explanation: Demurrage is the charge for detaining a ship beyond the agreed loading/unloading time.

questions.stem: A person who undertakes any risk in insurance business is known as
questions.explanation: An underwriter accepts (underwrites) risks in return for premium; a broker only arranges cover.

questions.stem: The main purpose of insurance is to
options: encourage business to survive and grow
ensure that facilities are available for operations
accept risks and extend credits to policy holders
spread individual losses over all covered participants
questions.explanation: Insurance pools premiums so that the losses of the few are shared by the many.

questions.stem: Bank giro is a system where
options: commercial banks can give loans to all customers
a central bank opens accounts for commercial banks
a customer uses a cheque to pay several bills
a customer closes his account by writing a cheque
questions.explanation: Under the bank giro (credit transfer), one cheque plus a list settles payments to several creditors.

questions.stem: Commercial banks are referred to as departmental stores of banking because they
questions.explanation: Like a department store, a commercial bank offers a wide range of financial services under one roof.

questions.stem: A market where new shares are traded is known as
questions.explanation: New issues are sold on the primary market; existing securities trade on the secondary market.

questions.stem: When a firm speaks of stock appreciation, it refers to
options: changes in the value of its stock resulting from price movements
increase in the price of its shares quoted on the stock exchange
an unexpected increase in the demand for its stocks
the value of its stocks in the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Stock appreciation is the rise in value of inventories held due to price increases.

questions.stem: When a vendor supplies newspapers from house to house and across the streets, the element of marketing mix involved is
questions.explanation: Getting the product to where customers are is the place (distribution) element.

questions.stem: When old customers stick to the old place to buy goods and services, it is known as
questions.explanation: Patronage (patronage motive) is the habitual buying from the same seller.

questions.stem: The most important piece of legislation governing business and commercial activities in Nigeria currently is the
options: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Decree, 1991
questions.explanation: The Companies and Allied Matters Decree 1990 (CAMA) is the principal law regulating businesses in Nigeria.

questions.stem: One of the criteria for differentiating consumer markets from industrial ones is the
questions.explanation: Industrial demand is derived demand, while consumer demand is direct.

questions.stem: The over-riding objective of the food and drug act in Nigeria is to prevent the
options: importation of food and drugs that can be locally manufactured
consumption of food and drugs not tested by the ministries of health
adulteration of food and drugs sold in the country
manufacturers of food and drugs from charging excessive prices
questions.explanation: The Food and Drugs Act protects consumers by prohibiting adulterated or unwholesome food and drugs.

questions.stem: The activities of consumers association in Nigeria have not been effective because
options: the government is not favourably disposed towards consumerism
there is poor enlightenment about consumer rights
the consumers have no medium for expressing their feelings
questions.explanation: Most consumers are unaware of their rights, so consumer associations get little support.

questions.stem: The main objective of a trade association can best be described as promoting and protecting
questions.explanation: A trade association exists to promote and protect the common interests of its members.

questions.stem: The management function of evaluating whether objectives are being achieved is
questions.explanation: Controlling compares actual performance with plans and takes corrective action.

questions.stem: In a business organization, the annual operation plan or budget is a form of
questions.explanation: A plan covering one year or less is short-term.

questions.stem: A key advantage of delegation is that
options: workers are prepared for higher responsibilities
the manager has less work to do
the manager spends less time on planning
the organization grows larger in size
questions.explanation: Delegation trains subordinates and prepares them for higher responsibility.

questions.stem: Social responsibility of business requires enterprises to
options: hold annual social parties for the public
draw their workers only from the immediate environment
address themselves to issues relating to the society
set up social welfare centres in their areas of operation
questions.explanation: Social responsibility means a business attends to the needs and concerns of the society in which it operates.

questions.stem: The existing system of governance and the administrative sub-divisions of a country which affect the operations of business in the country is described as
questions.explanation: The system of government and administrative structure form the political environment of business.

questions.stem: Sudden technological changes can have the effect of making
options: the control mechanism difficult to implement
the motivational factors in the company difficult to monitor
questions.explanation: New technology can quickly render existing products obsolete.

questions.stem: Which of the following contributed least to the evolution of commercial activities in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Money, banks and transport were the key drivers of commercial growth; traders' unions contributed least.

questions.stem: Extractive industries may also be denominated as
questions.explanation: Extraction is primary production, so extractive industries are primary industries.

questions.stem: The primary objective of a business organization is to
options: cater for the needs of its owners
assist the government to serve the citizens
improve the standard of living of its proprietors
